# Report: video14, L1 proxy, Three.js sampled-frame baseline (round 001)

Level: L1 (proxy). This is the Three.js sampled-frame baseline. It is not equivalent to the Blender CineRecon protocol.

What the 24 samples show: one continuous helmet-cam POV shot of an urban downhill mountain-bike run with no cuts. The rider's own handlebar, white gloves, black sleeves, red fork and front tyre stay in the lower part of the frame throughout. In order, the course goes: a wide asphalt start area with cones and spectators (0-1.1 s); a narrow alley with a white corrugated fence on the right and a crowd behind Red Bull banners on the left (about 1.4 s); a steep narrow path beside cream, brick, grey and graffiti walls on the right, with a crowd on a lower street to the left and a hedge (2-4.8 s); a left merge onto a road (about 5.5 s); a long asphalt descent with barriers and a crowd on the left and a stone wall on the right (6.2-10.3 s); a curved wooden berm/wall ride at about 11-11.8 s, with a strong camera lean; a blurry drop or jump at about 12.4 s; and a steep cobblestone street with barriers and a crowd on both sides and colourful houses (13.1-15.9 s).

Geometry: the course is a precomputed analytic centreline (heading and grade integrated per segment) built from 2 m chunks. Each chunk is made of box, cylinder and sphere proxies for the road surface, metal barriers, spectators (body cylinder plus head sphere, seeded colours), walls with zone colours, houses, a hedge, an inclined wooden berm, trees and cones. Distant city blocks are boxes. The sky is a flat blue background.

Rider rig: a rider group follows the path. It carries a bike sub-group (tyre torus, fork, stem, bar, gloves, arms) and the camera (vertical FOV 80, at head height). The head yaw and pitch, rider lean, camera roll, berm lateral offset and jump elevation are keyed at the sample times and smoothly interpolated. Arc-length progress is keyed piecewise-linearly, at about 6-8.5 m/s. update() is absolute in time and deterministic.

Inference vs observation: the zone boundaries, path curvature, speeds, roll and lean angles and berm geometry are estimated from the samples. Motion between samples is inferred.

Feedback: none received yet; this is the initial render candidate.

rounds.reason: Fix bike cockpit composition, ground gaps, scale of houses/crowd, berm and pitch
